newsitem.title: USA: IBM stock rises on upgrade, Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: IBM stock rises on upgrade, Dow rally.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp.'s stock rose in heavy trading Friday after Merrill Lynch said it could reach the $150-level in 12 months and SoundView Financial issued a more upbeat view for technology stocks.
IBM rose $4.875 to $122.125 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most active issues on volume of more than 4 million shares in late trading.
"People are starting to take another look at technology," one trader said. "And IBM is the No. 1 tech stock."
IBM also benefited as the stock market rallied after the government reported more proof that inflation is well under control, which eased worries over an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.

Merrill Lynch could not be reached for comment, but traders said the Wall Street firm strongly recommended buying IBM shares for short-term gains, upgrading it from accumulate previously. It maintained its long-term strong buy rating on the stock.
The brokerage expects IBM's new mainframes and disk drives to reach meaningful volumes in the third and fourth quarters, traders said.
SoundView said that technology stocks, which have been laggards, are poised as a group to outperform the broad market once again.

IBM's shares have been moribund this year and more so since this summer's technology stock meltdown. IBM trades at a very low price/earnings ratio for technology stocks, currently around 11 times 1996 earnings estimates.
But two weeks ago, IBM shares jumped 3-1/2 in one day to 115-1/4, after Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones raised his rating to a strong buy from a buy, with a 12-month price target of $145.
